commons.title: Bangunan Lumbung Padi Tradisional Warga Baduy.jpg
commons.description: Baduy residents store the grain from the huma rice harvest in the barn for supplies because they consider it taboo to buy and sell rice or unhulled rice. The barns are divided into two groups, one group in the east, another group across the river or towards the North. The place for pounding rice is in the north or on the river bank.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption identifies a Baduy rice barn; image visibly shows traditional Baduy architecture.

commons.title: Dari Balik Jendela Rumah Tradisional Warga Baduy Luar 1.jpg
commons.description: The Baduy tribe, the original tribe of the Banten community, is located in the mountains and lives in the Sulah Nyanda traditional house made of wood and bamboo. The making of the traditional house of the Baduy tribe is carried out by mutual cooperation using raw materials derived from nature and made from wood which is used to build the foundation. At the base of the foundation using a river stone or umpak with a floor made of split bamboo reinforced with a wooden frame and walls made of woven bamboo. Not all residents' houses have windows.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption identifies a Baduy Luar traditional house; image visibly shows its wood-and-bamboo architecture.
